speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the location and character of your headache, and have you noticed any other neurological symptoms like weakness or numbness?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your age and the combination of headache with worsening vision, I need to ask if you have experienced any jaw pain when chewing, scalp tenderness, or shoulder/hip stiffness. Additionally, have you noticed any double vision or drooping of the eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience jaw pain when chewing, scalp tenderness, or stiffness in your shoulders and hips? I also need to know if you have noticed any double vision or drooping of your eyelids.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given your age and symptoms, Giant Cell Arteritis is a strong concern, so I need to check for inflammation markers. REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal inflammatory markers make Giant Cell Arteritis unlikely, so we must look for other causes of your headache and vision loss. Have you noticed any changes in your vision field, such as blind spots, or any pain specifically behind your eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. No recent travel or sick contacts. No changes in hearing. Denies neck stiffness or photophobia.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to examine your eyes to check for papilledema or other signs of increased intracranial pressure. Please look straight ahead while I shine a light into your pupils to assess their reaction and check your visual fields for any blind spots.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. No recent travel or sick contacts. No changes in hearing. Denies neck stiffness or photophobia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The physical exam reveals bilateral papilledema, which is a critical finding. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI_with_contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRI rules out a mass or structural lesion, so we must investigate vascular causes like venous sinus thrombosis or idiopathic intracranial hypertension. REQUEST TEST: MR_Venography.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal MRI and MR Venography ruling out structural and vascular causes, I suspect Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension despite the atypical age. I will perform a lumbar puncture to measure the opening pressure. REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_Puncture_Opening_Pressure.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal opening pressure rules out Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension, so with papilledema and visual loss but normal structural and inflammatory workups, I suspect a compressive lesion on the optic nerves. DIAGNOSIS READY: Optic Nerve Glioma
